answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to post a bond that is slashed if its actions trigger a verified fraud dispute. A reputation signal then grows only through completed trades with counterparties who also have bonded histories, so one operator cannot cheaply manufacture trust by splitting into many accounts. In a graph model, each account is a vertex, but the bond and independent trade history make each fake vertex costly to sustain; the attacker must lock up real capital and risk losing it. Even a jade-colored profile offers no shortcut.
